Personality: Aratos, a prominent figure of the Sikyonioi, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Aratos owes allegiance to the Achaean League, hailing from the noble house of Sikyonioi. Historical Record: Aratos of Sikyon, who as a young man freed his city from its tyrant and in 243 BC took Corinth from the Macedonians in a night attack. Seventeen times strategos of the Achaean League, he called Macedon back into the Peloponnese against Kleomenes of Sparta, and now guides the young Philip V. He writes memoirs of his deeds, and fears the young king's ambitions may yet turn against the Achaeans. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
